description: Shared MongoDB contract fixture between fivenines-agent and fivenines-server (agent #258, server #493). Source of truth: fivenines-agent tests/fixtures/mongodb_contract_payload.json, asserted end-to-end by tests/test_mongodb.py::test_contract_fixture_round_trip: only the pymongo client is replaced (command in, reply or exception out, see mock_contract) and mongodb_metrics(**config['mongodb']) must equal payload['mongodb']. The server keeps a BYTE-IDENTICAL copy and posts each scenario's payload under data['mongodb']; the Rust port uses it as its parity source. Change the payload shape only in lockstep. Replies marked CAPTURED were recorded on 2026-11-02 from official MongoDB builds (4.2.25, 4.4.1, 4.4.31, 6.0.29, 7.0.45, 8.0.34) by the agent itself, see lab; they are trimmed to the fields the agent reads (serverStatus) and stripped of $clusterTime, operationTime and the election metrics, host names rewritten (db1.internal...). Each CAPTURED payload equals what the agent produced live against that mongod. SYNTHETIC replies say so; member_down's payload is issue #258's example, verbatim.
_agent_min_version_note: First agent release carrying the mongodb collector. Purely config-driven: an older agent ignores the top-level 'mongodb' key entirely (the key is absent from its payload), so the server may send it before the fleet upgrades. config['mongodb'] defaults to false server-side.

config_contract._note: config['mongodb'] is a TOP-LEVEL key, splatted into mongodb_metrics(**config['mongodb']), which takes **_kwargs: a key added later is ignored by this agent rather than raising a TypeError (the splat hazard). false disables the collector. Send every key explicitly, null included. Cross-OS (pure network): no capability gate, no OS gate, never stripped for Windows. Push a host's config to the agent ON that host: each agent reads only its own mongod, and the server merges the members' views.
config_contract.host: Default '127.0.0.1' (null or '' too): the mongod on the agent's own machine, over TCP -- what the setup guide documents. A host name (letters, digits, '-', '_', dots) or an IP literal (an IPv6 one with or without brackets), nothing else: no scheme, port, userinfo, path, comma (a seed list) or query, and no name ending in .sock. Or an absolute unix socket path ending in .sock (at most 107 bytes), percent-encoded into the URI; mongod creates its socket mode 0700, so the fivenines user usually cannot use it. Anything else is config_error before any connection. On an OS without unix sockets (Windows) a socket path is config_error.
config_contract.port: Default 27017 (null or '' too); 1-65535. Ignored for a unix socket.
config_contract.username: null or '' = no authentication (a mongod without security.authorization). Otherwise the user to authenticate as.
config_contract.password: The user's password. Never logged, removed from every shipped error message. A username without a password is config_error (the driver refuses it).
config_contract.auth_source: Default 'admin' (null or '' too). Ignored for MONGODB-X509 (always $external).
config_contract.auth_mechanism: null = negotiate (SCRAM-SHA-256, else SCRAM-SHA-1). Accepted: SCRAM-SHA-1, SCRAM-SHA-256, MONGODB-X509 (any case). Anything else is config_error: PLAIN would send the password in clear, and GSSAPI / MONGODB-AWS / MONGODB-OIDC need libraries the agent does not bundle. MONGODB-X509 authenticates with tls_certificate_key_file and needs tls true (else config_error); username is then optional (the server derives it from the certificate subject).
config_contract.tls: Only an explicit true (true/1/'true'/'yes'/'on') enables TLS; default false.
config_contract.tls_ca_file: PEM CA bundle to verify the mongod certificate with. null = the agent's bundled public CA set (certifi), NOT the OS trust store (what the OS store resolves to inside the binary depends on the OpenSSL it bundles): a certificate from an internal CA needs this. A file that does not load is config_error. A path that is not a regular file (a FIFO, a device, a directory) is config_error before the driver opens it.
config_contract.tls_certificate_key_file: PEM client certificate + key (MONGODB-X509, or a mongod with net.tls.allowConnectionsWithoutCertificates false). A file that does not load is config_error. An encrypted (passphrase-protected) key is not supported: the agent passes an explicit empty passphrase, so OpenSSL never prompts on a terminal and such a key fails to load (config_error). A path that is not a regular file is config_error, as for tls_ca_file.
config_contract.tls_allow_invalid_certificates: Only an explicit true disables certificate verification (and the CA set is then not loaded). Default false. The mongod certificate must otherwise name `host`: with host 127.0.0.1, a certificate issued for db1.internal fails with tls_error -- configure the name the certificate carries.
config_contract.connection: One client per tick, closed in a finally: MongoClient(host, port, directConnection=True, appname='fivenines-agent', serverSelectionTimeoutMS=5000, connectTimeoutMS=5000, socketTimeoutMS=10000, maxPoolSize=1, retryReads=False, retryWrites=False, serverMonitoringMode='poll', + auth/tls). Never SRV, never a seed list, never directConnection=False: the agent never connects to another member. Each tick opens two connections (the driver's monitor + one for the commands), each logged by mongod.
config_contract.bounds: The hello gate (server selection + connection + authentication + hello) is bounded at 5s; each later command at min(10s, what is left of a 15s budget), via pymongo.timeout(); a section the budget no longer covers reads timeout. The whole collection runs on a worker abandoned after 20s (what no driver timeout covers): that tick reports timeout, and so does every later one until that worker returns (no second collection starts behind it). The driver's own monitor thread resolves and dials the host outside both bounds and outlives a closed client while blocked (a resolver that never answers): no client is built while such a thread from an earlier tick is still alive once given 1s to end (close() does not join them: one merely exiting is waited for), so a stuck resolver costs one thread, and every tick reports timeout ('a previous MongoDB connection attempt is still blocked ...') until it ends.

privilege_contract._note: clusterMonitor on admin covers hello, serverStatus, replSetGetStatus and replSetGetConfig on every role; read on local adds the oplog read. read on local is OPTIONAL and broad: it lets the account read the oplog's contents (every recent write to every database), although the agent only asks for the first and last entries' ts. Without it only the oplog section reads not_authorized. Every command is read-only: never dbStats, listDatabases, collStats, currentOp, the profiler, or anything that writes.
privilege_contract.setup: db.getSiblingDB('admin').createUser({user: 'fivenines', pwd: passwordPrompt(), roles: [{role: 'clusterMonitor', db: 'admin'}, {role: 'read', db: 'local'}]}) -- on a replica set, on the primary (the user replicates to every member); on a sharded cluster, once through mongos for the routers and once on each shard's and the config server set's primary for their members (shard-local users).
privilege_contract.missing_privilege: A user without one of them is NOT an error envelope: hello needs no privilege, so the agent is connected and authenticated (reachable true) and each refused command drops only its section (collection.errors[section] = 'not_authorized').
privilege_contract.arbiter: An arbiter stores no users: with credentials configured, its authentication fails. The agent recognises the arbiter from the driver's unauthenticated monitor hello and reports role arbiter (scenario arbiter_self_auth_on), never auth_failed.

envelope_contract._note: data['mongodb'] is NEVER null. Its keys are always exactly: reachable, error_type, error_message, process, role, version, me, collection, node, replica_set, sharding.
envelope_contract.failure: reachable false ONLY when the hello gate fails: the connection, the TLS handshake or the authentication (and the closed error_types below). error_type and error_message are then set and every other key is null.
envelope_contract.success: reachable true, error_type and error_message null, process and role set. Once connected and authenticated, a refused command drops ONLY its section: its collection flag goes false and collection.errors[section] says why. reachable stays true.
envelope_contract.error_message: At most 500 characters, redacted (logs.redact), never the configured password (of 6 characters or more: a shorter one would only garble a message). For a connection failure it is the driver monitor's own error (stable from tick to tick), never the server selection's message (which embeds a random topology id). For a server error it is the server's errmsg, without the reply dump.

error_types.connection_refused: Nothing usable answered: connection refused, a host name that does not resolve, no route, or a connection closed or reset before the handshake -- a plain client against a requireTLS mongod reads this way ('connection closed', measured: nothing in the error says TLS). Server status: unreachable.
error_types.timeout: The connection or the hello timed out (a hung or blackholed mongod, or no answer within the 5s server selection), or the collection outlived its 20s bound. Server status: unreachable. Also while the driver's monitor thread from an earlier tick is still blocked (config_contract.bounds).
error_types.tls_error: The TLS handshake failed: certificate not verified (a private CA with tls_ca_file null, a host name or IP address the certificate does not carry -- both measured), protocol mismatch. Server status: config_error.
error_types.auth_failed: The authentication failed: AuthenticationFailed (18: wrong user, password or auth_source, or an X.509 username the certificate does not match), UserNotFound (11: an X.509 certificate subject with no user in $external), MechanismUnavailable (334: a mechanism the user has no credentials for, e.g. SCRAM-SHA-256 forced for a SCRAM-SHA-1-only user). All measured. Server status: config_error.
error_types.server_too_old: MongoDB older than 4.4 (wire version < 9): the driver refuses it before any command. Server status: config_error.
error_types.config_error: The config is invalid (host, port, auth_mechanism, X509 without TLS, a username without password, a TLS file that does not load). Nothing was sent. Server status: config_error. So is a value Python cannot convert (a port of 1e400, a socket path that is not valid UTF-8) and any failure of the validation no rule anticipated: the envelope is never null.
error_types.shutting_down: The mongod answered ShutdownInProgress (91) or InterruptedAtShutdown (11600). Server status: unreachable.
error_types.unknown: Anything else, including a hello answered with another server error. Server status: unreachable. A peer that does not speak the MongoDB wire protocol reads unknown with a fixed message.

collection_contract._note: collection = {server_status_ok, repl_status_ok, repl_config_ok, oplog_ok, errors}. A flag is true when its section was read, false when it was refused or failed (and errors[section] says why), null when the section does not apply to the role. errors keys: server_status, repl_status, repl_config, oplog; values: not_authorized (Unauthorized, 13), refused (any other server error), timeout (a driver or server timeout, or the 15s budget spent before the command could be sent), error (anything else: the connection dropped mid-tick, an unexpected reply).
collection_contract.required_sections: The server decides which sections it requires: serverStatus everywhere, plus replSetGetStatus and replSetGetConfig on a member. A refused oplog read is a warning only.

by_role.arbiter: all four null, node null (hello only).
by_role.uninitiated: server_status_ok set; repl_config_ok and oplog_ok null; repl_status_ok null when replSetGetStatus answered NotYetInitialized (94), false with errors.repl_status when it could not be read (refused, timed out, failed): the role then rests on hello alone, where an uninitiated and a removed node look alike.
by_role.removed: server_status_ok set; repl_status_ok null (a removed node has no view of the set: replSetGetStatus answers InvalidReplicaSetConfig and nothing else), repl_config_ok set; oplog_ok null.

collection_contract.direct_shard_connection: MEASURED on 8.0.34 and 7.0.45 with two shards: a direct connection to a shard member refuses none of the agent's commands (all target admin and local) and logs no direct-connection warning, so a shard member reports like any replica set member.

field_contract.role: From hello, then replSetGetStatus: mongos (hello msg isdbgrid); arbiter (arbiterOnly: stop after hello); otherwise, when hello has setName or isreplicaset, replSetGetStatus decides: NotYetInitialized (94) = uninitiated (rs.initiate() never run), InvalidReplicaSetConfig (93) = removed (MEASURED on 4.4 to 8.0: a removed node answers hello exactly like an uninitiated one, isreplicaset without setName), any other answer = replica_set_member (when hello names no set and replSetGetStatus could not be read, uninitiated, with errors.repl_status saying why). No setName nor isreplicaset: standalone.
field_contract.version: serverStatus().version; null when serverStatus was not read, and on an arbiter.
field_contract.me: hello's me (host:port as the set's config spells it); null off replica set members.
field_contract.node: An object on every role except the arbiter (null there). Values as MongoDB reports them, renamed to snake_case; cumulative counters stay cumulative (the server rate()s them; the agent never diffs). A field this version, engine or process does not have is null, never 0; when serverStatus was not read every field but oplog is null (node keeps its shape).
field_contract.node.opcounters / node.opcounters_repl: opcounters / opcountersRepl, {insert, query, update, delete, getmore, command}. opcounters_repl null where MongoDB omits it (mongos).
field_contract.node.wiredtiger: wiredTiger.cache: 'bytes currently in the cache', 'maximum bytes configured', 'tracked dirty bytes in the cache', 'pages read into cache', 'pages written from cache'. null on mongos, an arbiter, or another storage engine.
field_contract.node.tickets: queues.execution.{read,write}.{out,available} (8.0+, the rename), else wiredTiger.concurrentTransactions; null when neither exists (mongos).
field_contract.node.global_lock: globalLock.currentQueue.{readers,writers} and globalLock.activeClients.{readers,writers}; null where MongoDB omits globalLock (mongos).
field_contract.node.op_latencies: opLatencies.{reads,writes,commands}.{latency (cumulative microseconds), ops}: the server derives the average latency as a ratio of rates.
field_contract.node.oplog: {window_s}: the first and last local.oplog.rs entries ($natural 1 then -1, limit 1, projection {ts: 1}), window_s = last.ts.time - first.ts.time. null off data-bearing replica set members, or when the read was refused (oplog_ok false).
field_contract.replica_set: An object for role replica_set_member and removed, null otherwise. Fields from a command that failed are null (its collection flag is false); set_name falls back to the config's _id, then hello's setName.
field_contract.replica_set.replica_set_id: replSetGetConfig settings.replicaSetId as 24 lowercase hex characters: THE key the server merges the members' views on. null when absent (sets initiated before MongoDB 3.2: group by set_name) or when the config was not read.
field_contract.replica_set.configsvr: replSetGetConfig configsvr (absent = false): a config server set.
field_contract.replica_set.term: replSetGetStatus term: when two members' views disagree on the PRIMARY, the higher term is the current one (isolated_primary vs new_primary_after_failover).
field_contract.replica_set.my_state / my_state_str: replSetGetStatus myState and the self member's stateStr. removed: only what the 93 reply reports -- MongoDB 4.4 to 8.0 report nothing, so both null.
field_contract.replica_set.members[]: One entry per member of the config (of the status when the config was not read), merged by _id AND host (a reconfig between the two reads can give a replaced member's _id to a new host: its status fields then stay null), sorted by name, at most 50 (MongoDB's own maximum). null when neither command was read, and for a removed node (it has no view of the set).
field_contract.members[].id / name: _id / the config's host (the status' name when the config was not read).
field_contract.members[].self: The status entry's self flag; null when the status was not read.
field_contract.members[].health / state / state_str / u: Verbatim from the status entry; state is the integer, state_str the verbatim string -- never a closed enum.
field_contract.members[].ping_ms: pingMs; null for self and for a member whose health is not 1 (its last ping is stale).
field_contract.members[].last_heartbeat_age_s / last_he: The reply's own date minus lastHeartbeat / lastHeartbeatRecv, whole seconds, clamped at 0: the mongod's clock, never the agent's. null for self, and for the zero date (never). lastHeartbeat is stamped on a FAILED heartbeat too, so for a down member it is the last attempt and lastHeartbeatRecv the last heartbeat it sent.
field_contract.members[].config_version: The status entry's configVersion: -1 for a member this node has not heard from since it started; a member that went down keeps the version it last reported (member_down_captured).
field_contract.members[].priority / votes / hidden / ar: The config entry, verbatim (priority may be fractional); null when the config was not read.
field_contract.members[].secondary_delay_s: The config entry's secondaryDelaySecs, or slaveDelay before 5.0.
field_contract.sharding: {config_server_set}: the set name before the / of serverStatus().sharding.configsvrConnectionString -- on a shard member the cluster's config server set (how the server groups the sets of one sharded cluster), on a config server member its own set, on a mongos the cluster it routes to. null when serverStatus carries none (not sharded, or not read).

lag_contract._note: lag_s is computed inside ONE replSetGetStatus reply, never against a clock.
lag_contract.reference: The PRIMARY's optimeDate in this reply (the freshest, should the reply list more than one). With no primary, the freshest optimeDate among the members that have a lag (below) -- the mongosh algorithm.
lag_contract.value: lag_s = reference - member.optimeDate, whole seconds, clamped at 0. The primary is 0.
lag_contract.null_for: an arbiter (no optime); a member whose health is not 1 (MongoDB resets its optime to Timestamp(0, 0): a naive lag reads 56 years); a member in STARTUP (0), STARTUP2 (5, initial sync), UNKNOWN (6), ARBITER (7), DOWN (8) or REMOVED (10); a zero or missing optimeDate; and every member when no reference exists.
lag_contract.delayed_members: A delayed member's lag_s includes its secondary_delay_s by design: compare the two before calling it lagging.

mock_contract._note: Agent-side inputs; the server ignores 'config' and 'mongo'. Each scenario's 'mongo' maps what the agent sends to what it gets back, in MongoDB Extended JSON (relaxed), decoded as MongoClient decodes BSON (naive UTC datetimes). The test fails if the agent sends anything a scenario does not list, or does not send something it lists.
mock_contract.oplog: {first, last}: the two find_one reads of local.oplog.rs, or {raises: <exception>}.
mock_contract.monitor: What the driver's own monitor saw: hello (its unauthenticated reply, delivered through the heartbeat listener; the server description carries its maxWireVersion) and error (the error the monitor recorded for the server: what a ServerSelectionTimeoutError hides). Kept for the scenarios whose hello fails, and for arbiter_self_auth_on.
mock_contract.exception: {type: a pymongo.errors class name (or SSLCertVerificationError), reply: the server's ok:0 reply for OperationFailure and its subclasses and for NotPrimaryError, message: the text for the others}.

lab._note: How the CAPTURED scenarios were produced, so they can be re-run: official tarballs on Debian 12 (4.x/6.0 with Debian 11's libssl1.1), every node with a keyFile (or --auth for a standalone), users created through the localhost exception, then the real collector run with the privilege_contract user while every reply it received was recorded.
lab.replica_set: 3 members, priority 2 on db1, settings heartbeatTimeoutSecs 2 / electionTimeoutMillis 3000. member_down: SIGKILL db3. no_primary: SIGKILL db2 too. isolated_primary: electionTimeoutMillis 60000, SIGSTOP db2 and db3 (from db1, a partition). new_primary_after_failover: SIGKILL the primary. delayed_hidden_member: reconfig db3 to priority 0, hidden, secondaryDelaySecs (slaveDelay on 4.4) 3600. psa_with_arbiter: setDefaultRWConcern w:1 (5.0+ refuses the reconfig otherwise), then add an arbiter. initial_sync: a new member started with the initialSyncHangBeforeCopyingDatabases failpoint. removed_self: reconfig without db3.
lab.sharded: 8.0 (and 7.0, same results): a 1-member config server set, two 1-member shard sets, one mongos; cluster users created through mongos, shard-local users on the shard.
lab.tls: 7.0 with --tlsMode requireTLS, a server certificate from a private CA naming DNS:localhost only, --tlsAllowConnectionsWithoutCertificates, and an X.509 client certificate from the same CA.
lab.all_versions: Every replica set scenario ran on 4.4.31, 6.0.29, 7.0.45 and 8.0.34 with the same outcome; the fixture keeps the 7.0 captures, plus the version-specific ones.

standalone.description: CAPTURED from a real MongoDB 7.0.45 (a standalone mongod with --auth). serverStatus only: repl_* and oplog_ok null (do not apply), replica_set and sharding null, me null (a standalone's hello has none).

replset_primary_view.description: CAPTURED from a real MongoDB 7.0.45 (a 3-member set with a keyFile, seen from db1, the PRIMARY). self carries no ping and no heartbeat ages; the primary's lag_s is 0 by construction.

members.name: db1.internal:27017
members.infoMessage: Could not find member to sync from

replset_secondary_view.description: CAPTURED from a real MongoDB 7.0.45 (the same set seen from db2, a SECONDARY). same replica_set_id as replset_primary_view: the server keeps ONE view of the set.

member_down.description: SYNTHETIC (shaped like member_down_captured): db2's view with db3 down -- issue #258's example payload, verbatim. MongoDB resets a health-0 member's optime to Timestamp(0, 0) (optimeDate 1970), so its lag_s is null rather than 56 years; it keeps a stale pingMs 0, so ping_ms is null; last_heartbeat_age_s is the last ATTEMPT (MongoDB stamps lastHeartbeat on a failed heartbeat too), last_heartbeat_recv_age_s the last heartbeat db3 sent before it went down; configVersion -1 is what a member not heard from since this node started reports.

members.name: db3.internal:27017
members.lastHeartbeatMessage: Error connecting to db3.internal:27017 :: caused by :: Connection refused

member_down_captured.description: CAPTURED from a real MongoDB 7.0.45 (db3 killed with SIGKILL, seen from db2). the down member keeps the configVersion it last reported (1 here) and a pingMs of 0, which ships as null.

members.name: db3.internal:27017
members.lastHeartbeatMessage: Error connecting to db3.internal:27017 :: caused by :: onInvoke :: caused by :: Connection refused

no_primary.description: CAPTURED from a real MongoDB 7.0.45 (db2 and db3 killed, seen from db1). db1 stepped down to SECONDARY (no majority): with no PRIMARY in the reply, lag_s is measured from the freshest healthy data-bearing member (db1 itself, 0).

members.name: db1.internal:27017
members.infoMessage: Could not find member to sync from

members.name: db2.internal:27017
members.lastHeartbeatMessage: Error connecting to db2.internal:27017 :: caused by :: onInvoke :: caused by :: Connection refused

members.name: db3.internal:27017
members.lastHeartbeatMessage: no response within election timeout period

isolated_primary.description: CAPTURED from a real MongoDB 7.0.45 (db2 and db3 frozen with SIGSTOP while db1 is PRIMARY, with electionTimeoutMillis 60000 and heartbeatTimeoutSecs 2: from db1 this is a network partition, in the seconds before it steps down). db1 still claims PRIMARY under its term and sees db2 and db3 down. The other side's view (new_primary_after_failover) carries a higher term: the server must prefer the view with the highest term, not believe every self-declared PRIMARY.

members.infoMessage: Could not find member to sync from

members.name: db2.internal:27017
members.lastHeartbeatMessage: Couldn't get a connection within the time limit

members.name: db3.internal:27017
members.lastHeartbeatMessage: Couldn't get a connection within the time limit

new_primary_after_failover.description: CAPTURED from a real MongoDB 7.0.45 (db1, the primary, killed with SIGKILL; seen from db3, which won the election). term 3 > the down db1's last view; db2 now syncs from db3.

members.name: db1.internal:27017
members.lastHeartbeatMessage: Error connecting to db1.internal:27017 :: caused by :: onInvoke :: caused by :: Connection refused

members.name: db3.internal:27017
members.infoMessage: Could not find member to sync from

delayed_hidden_member.description: CAPTURED from a real MongoDB 7.0.45 (db3's own view after a reconfig to secondaryDelaySecs 3600, hidden, priority 0). its lag_s grows towards secondary_delay_s by design (a few seconds here, right after the reconfig): the server compares the two before calling it lagging.

psa_with_arbiter.description: CAPTURED from a real MongoDB 7.0.45 (the set with an arbiter added, seen from the primary). the arbiter's status entry has no optime at all, so its lag_s is null; arbiter_only comes from the config.

arbiter_self.description: CAPTURED from a real MongoDB 7.0.45 (the agent on the arbiter, configured without credentials). hello only: an arbiter stores no users, so with auth on nothing else is readable; its state reaches the server through the data-bearing members' views.

arbiter_self_auth_on.description: CAPTURED from a real MongoDB 7.0.45 (the agent on the arbiter, configured WITH the credentials that work on the data-bearing members). its authenticated hello fails with AuthenticationFailed (the arbiter has no users), but the driver's own UNAUTHENTICATED monitor hello says arbiterOnly, so the payload is the arbiter's, not auth_failed.

initial_sync.description: CAPTURED from a real MongoDB 7.0.45 (db4 added while held in its initial sync (STARTUP2) by the initialSyncHangBeforeCopyingDatabases failpoint; seen from the primary). its lag_s is null rather than whatever it has copied so far.

removed_self.description: CAPTURED from a real MongoDB 7.0.45 (db3 after a reconfig removed it). MEASURED on 4.4, 6.0, 7.0 and 8.0 alike: a removed node answers hello exactly like an uninitiated one (isreplicaset, no setName, no me) and replSetGetStatus with InvalidReplicaSetConfig (93) and NO state -- that code is what tells it from an uninitiated node (94). role removed: replica_set names the set from the config it still holds (so the server can say which set dropped the host), my_state null (not reported), members null (no view of the set); repl_status_ok and oplog_ok null.

hello.info: Does not have a valid replica set config

reply.errmsg: Our replica set config is invalid or we are not a member of it

uninitiated.description: CAPTURED from a real MongoDB 7.0.45 (a mongod started with --replSet, rs.initiate() never run, no access control). hello says isreplicaset without setName and replSetGetStatus answers NotYetInitialized (94): role uninitiated, the repl sections and the oplog do not apply (null), replica_set null.

hello.info: Does not have a valid replica set config

reply.errmsg: no replset config has been received

uninitiated_status_not_read.description: DERIVED from uninitiated (CAPTURED, 7.0.45) with replSetGetStatus replaced by the Unauthorized (13) answer captured in not_authorized (a user without clusterMonitor). hello cannot tell an uninitiated node from a removed one (isreplicaset, no setName), so the role rests on hello alone: uninitiated, with repl_status_ok false and errors.repl_status saying the status was not read. A timeout or a dropped connection reads the same way, with timeout or error.

reply.errmsg: not authorized on admin to execute command { replSetGetStatus: 1, lsid: { id: UUID("3fd15fe5-ebd6-4b50-b60f-5f4ee9db1fc0") }, $clusterTime: { clusterTime: Timestamp(1793633072, 33), signature: { hash: BinData(0, F7A1FBFDC3BD0DE6178CB020DF6D55DFF36C23E8), keyId: 7703595380969046022 } }, maxTimeMS: 9999, $db: "admin", $readPreference: { mode: "primaryPreferred" } }

pre_5_0_slave_delay.description: CAPTURED from a real MongoDB 4.4.31 (db3's own view after a reconfig to slaveDelay 3600, hidden, priority 0). before 5.0 the delay is the config's slaveDelay (renamed secondaryDelaySecs in 5.0): secondary_delay_s reads both.

ismaster_fallback.description: CAPTURED from a real MongoDB 4.4.1 (a 2-member set, seen from the primary). 4.4.0 and 4.4.1 predate the hello command: CommandNotFound (59), so the agent asks isMaster, whose reply says ismaster instead of isWritablePrimary.

shard_member_8_0.description: CAPTURED from a real MongoDB 8.0.34 (a member of shard1, in a 2-shard cluster, over a DIRECT connection with a shard-local user). MEASURED: 8.0 refuses none of the agent's commands on a direct connection to a shard member (they all target admin and local) and logs no direct-connection warning -- nor does 7.0. sharding.config_server_set names the config server set before the / of serverStatus().sharding.configsvrConnectionString: how the server groups the sets of one sharded cluster.

mongos.description: CAPTURED from a real MongoDB 8.0.34 (the cluster's mongos (hello msg isdbgrid)). serverStatus only. MEASURED nulls: no storage engine (wiredtiger, tickets), no opcountersRepl, no metrics.document, no metrics.cursor.open.noTimeout; sharding names the cluster it routes to.

version_6_concurrent_transactions.description: CAPTURED from a real MongoDB 6.0.29 (a standalone). the tickets come from wiredTiger.concurrentTransactions (as on 4.4 and 7.0, measured).

no_credentials.description: CAPTURED from a real MongoDB 7.0.45 (a standalone with --auth and an agent configured without credentials (username null)). hello needs no authentication, so reachable is true and serverStatus is refused (Unauthorized: 'requires authentication').

unix_socket.description: CAPTURED from a real MongoDB 7.0.45 (a standalone reached over its unix socket (path rewritten)). same payload as over TCP.

auth_failed.description: CAPTURED from a real MongoDB 7.0.45 (a wrong password). the authenticated hello fails with AuthenticationFailed (18) and the monitor's hello is no arbiter's: reachable false, auth_failed (server: config_error).

mechanism_unavailable.description: CAPTURED from a real MongoDB 7.0.45 (auth_mechanism SCRAM-SHA-256 for a user created with SCRAM-SHA-1 credentials only).
